# devin-office

> A local-first dashboard that renders live Devin CLI/Desktop sessions and subagents as an animated SVG circuit board in the browser.

Devin Office solves observability for Devin sessions: the Devin UI shows one session at a time, while this tool reads Devin's local session databases read-only and renders all active sessions, subagents, and tool calls as a live circuit-board view (a Devin chip with green traces to tools and subagent arms). It is for Devin CLI/Desktop users who want a single glanceable view of what their agents are doing right now. Everything runs on the local machine with Python's standard library only; no pip install, no build step, no telemetry. An optional split mode (probe + private hub) puts the dashboard on a second machine over a private network.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Icaro0310/devin-control/blob/main/packages/office/README.md): full documentation

## Key commands

- `devin-office --port 8788`: standalone read-only mode; serve the dashboard at http://localhost:8788 from the Devin machine (also `python3 src/devin_office/daemon.py --port 8788` from a checkout, no install)
- `devin-office-hub --port 8790`: split mode; serve the dashboard on a hub that receives probe state (token required for non-loopback binds)
- `devin-office-probe --interval 3`: split mode; poll local Devin state and POST changes to the hub
- `devin-office-executor`: optional ACP control process for message/spawn/kill (opt-in via OFFICE_CONTROL_ENABLED)
- `pip install -e packages/office`: install the console scripts from a checkout

## When to use / when not

- Use when: you run Devin CLI or Desktop locally and want live visibility into sessions, subagents, and tool activity; you want a dashboard with zero dependencies beyond Python 3.10+; you want a read-only observer that never writes to Devin's databases; you need the board on a second machine over a private network (split mode).
- Not when: you need historical search or analytics over past sessions (use devin-search or devin-metrics); you want to control sessions remotely without explicit opt-in (controls are disabled by default); you have no Devin CLI/Desktop install on the observed machine (there is nothing to read); you need a hosted or multi-user dashboard.
